mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% in two consecutive monthly releases
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically below the median market return at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decrease in both the federal funds rate and CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) by at least 0.3 percentage points signals a disinflationary easing cycle, which lowers real interest rates and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly change < -0.3% AND CPIAUCSL monthly change < -0.3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 units alongside an unemployment rate below 4% signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to margin compression.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above 5% YoY for six consecutive months signals a shift in household preferences away from consumption toward saving, which reduces aggregate demand and corporate revenues, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in both the GDP price index (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 0.5% signals a robust acceleration in demand and construction activity, which boosts corporate earnings and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change > 0.5% AND HOUST monthly change > 1000 units
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).
